title: MiniCPM-o 4.5: streaming batching, launch overlap and quality-constrained transfer
summary: Transfer hypotheses for streaming MiniCPM-o serving: measure complete audio delivery, preserve request-owned state, and qualify combined numerical changes separately from isolated kernels.

hardware: NVIDIA L20X source campaign; other devices need independent qualification
software: Dedicated single-GPU engine source snapshot; downstream vLLM-Omni and SGLang-Omni revisions must be checked independently
conditions: Fixed checkpoint bytes, sampling parameters, reference audio and workload across comparisons.
Separate tuning/evaluation requests and consistent warmup/cache policies.

claims.description: The source reports separating Token2Wav into an MPS worker, batching streaming windows, graph replay and asynchronous host-to-device preparation.
The measured fast profile is not quality-qualified: combining TF32 HiFT and batched setup exceeded a chunk error bound despite individual mechanisms passing their checks.
Several plausible launch reductions measured neutral or negative at service level, including larger HiFT graph buckets and asynchronous Token2Wav results.

downstream_impact: Inspect current vLLM-Omni implementation before porting: it may already provide fused CFM, cross-reference batching and graph replay absent from historical measurements.
Keep reference extraction, setup, decode, output delivery and queueing distinct when profiling.
MPS and graph bucket choices are device/workload tuning hypotheses, not universally optimal defaults.
recommendations: Report frames/s as 25 times delivered audio seconds divided by wall time, TTFA from first delivered samples, and request RTF from last delivered samples. Preserve chunk counts and failures.
Label a one-waveform response non-streaming; its TTFA is close to full-response latency and differs semantically from an incremental stream.
Compare lossless execution/configuration changes first; numerical precision, smaller first windows and sampling changes require separate quality qualification.
validation_plan: Pin source and dependency identities; verify that editable imports do not escape the tested checkout.
Run disjoint warmup and evaluation prompts at every reported concurrency; retain per-request audio, timing, failures and run-level variability.
Use numerical/state tests plus complete served WER, speaker similarity and quality scoring; test combinations, not just each mechanism alone.
Compare paired baseline/candidate service runs with equivalent caches and devices; keep microbench and imported results separate.
limitations: Source-backed import only; no locally verified downstream acceleration.
Historical vLLM-Omni plateau and SGLang non-streaming observations apply only to their pinned source campaign revisions.
A dedicated engine schedule cannot be transplanted as a deployment parameter; state and runtime ownership differ.
